name: ANSI/IEEE Photoelectric emitter-receiver switch form
aliases: IEEE Normally Open Emitter-Receiver - DC Driven
summary: IEEE-library form of photoelectric emitter-receiver switch: a photoelectric emitter-receiver device uses an optical path to determine a switching output.
description: This reference locates photoelectric emitter-receiver switch in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented photoelectric emitter/receiver switches family. A photoelectric emitter-receiver device uses an optical path to determine a switching output. The schematic needs the supply and output connections, while the layout defines the optical arrangement. The public library uses HPE11B16 for its horizontal representation; this is a vendor block name, not an IEEE standards symbol number.

Read the operating mechanism and the contact reference state together. Cross-reference every associated contact to the same device and show which movement, signal or reset changes its condition; the symbol alone does not establish the complete switching sequence.

Establish whether the indicated state corresponds to a received or interrupted beam. Optical detection is not the same sensing principle as inductive or capacitive proximity. The linked functional counterpart explains the same operating role in its own drawing context; agreement of every detailed convention mark is not asserted.
